findings.summary: Arch Linux is an open-source, rolling-release distribution designed for general-purpose use. It provides monthly installation media snapshots and is intentionally minimal, requiring user configuration during installation. The system is kept up-to-date by regularly updating individual software packages. Comprehensive community documentation is provided via the ArchWiki.

mechanisms.title: Package management via pacman
mechanisms.explanation: Pacman, a package manager written specifically for Arch Linux, handles the installation, removal, and updating of software packages. It interfaces with the libalpm back-end and supports repository package signing since Pacman 4.0.0, with mandatory signing for official packages as of March 2012.

mechanisms.title: Community-driven software repository (AUR)
mechanisms.explanation: The Arch User Repository (AUR) serves as a community-driven repository providing packages not included in official repositories and alternative versions. AUR packages can be built manually or installed through helper tools such as yay.
